title: Geometric integrality of an algebra can be tested on finite field extensions
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $S$ a commutative unital $k$-algebra. For a field extension $L/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], write $S\otimes_k L$ for the tensor product of the underlying $k$-vector spaces, with multiplication $(s\otimes a)(t\otimes b)=st\otimes ab$ and unit $1\otimes1$. An integral domain means a nonzero commutative ring in which $uv=0$ implies $u=0$ or $v=0$. If $S\otimes_k L$ is an integral domain for every finite field extension $L/k$ (finite means finite-dimensional as a $k$-vector space), then $S\otimes_k K$ is an integral domain for every field extension $K/k$. No finite-generation or Noetherian hypothesis on $S$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0FWF, algebra-lemma-characterize-geometrically-integral, implication (2) to (1); algebra-definition-geometrically-integral defines (1) by all field extensions.

proof.text: Take the degree-one extension $k/k$ in the hypothesis. The mutually inverse maps $S\otimes_k k\to S$, $s\otimes c\mapsto cs$, and $S\to S\otimes_k k$, $s\mapsto s\otimes1$, show that $S$ is a domain, hence $1_S\ne0$. Fix an arbitrary extension $K/k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector], choose a $k$-basis $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ of the underlying vector space of $S$ containing $1_S$.

source.place: Tag 0FWF, algebra-lemma-characterize-geometrically-integral (2) implies (1); agent coefficient-specialization proof, initialization.

proof.text: For each commutative $k$-algebra $T$, write $\lambda_i:S\to k$ for the coefficient of $e_i$. Every tensor has a unique finite expansion $\sum_i e_i\otimes t_i$: expand each first factor in a finite sum of basis vectors; uniqueness follows by applying the $k$-linear map $s\otimes t\mapsto\lambda_i(s)t$ for each $i$. These maps are defined by the balanced tensor relations. For a $k$-algebra homomorphism $f:T\to T\prime$, the map $1\otimes f$ therefore sends the coefficients $(t_i)$ to $(f(t_i))$ and is injective whenever $f$ is injective. Its multiplicativity follows on pure tensors from $(s\otimes t)(s\prime\otimes u)=ss\prime\otimes tu$ and extends by distributivity. In particular $S\otimes_k K$ is nonzero: the coefficient of the basis vector $1_S$ in $1_S\otimes1_K$ is $1_K\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 0FWF, algebra-lemma-characterize-geometrically-integral (2) implies (1); explicit elementary tensor-coordinate calculation.

proof.text: Suppose for contradiction that $x,y\in S\otimes_k K$ are nonzero and $xy=0$. Use Step 2 to write their finite coefficient families as $(a_i)$ and $(b_i)$, and choose $a_{i_0}\ne0$ and $b_{j_0}\ne0$. Let $A\subset K$ be the $k$-subalgebra generated by all these finitely many coefficients together with $a_{i_0}^{-1}$ and $b_{j_0}^{-1}$. It is nonzero, commutative, unital and finitely generated over $k$. The same finite sums define $x_A,y_A\in S\otimes_k A$ and map to $x,y$. Step 2 applied to $A\hookrightarrow K$ makes this tensor map injective, so $x_Ay_A=0$.

source.place: Tag 0FWF, algebra-lemma-characterize-geometrically-integral (2) implies (1); finite coefficient algebra with two inverted coefficients.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-maximal-ideal] to the nontrivial ring $A$ and choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. By [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-quotient-field], $L=A/\mathfrak m$ is a field. The composite $k\to A\to L$ is a unital field homomorphism and hence injective, giving an extension $L/k$ as in [def-pc-field-extension]. The images of the finite algebra generators of $A$ generate $L$ as a $k$-algebra: every residue class is the image of a polynomial in those generators. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma] applies and $L/k$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 00FV, algebra-theorem-nullstellensatz (1), applied to the finite type algebra A; maximal ideal and quotient-field leaves.

proof.text: Let $\bar x,\bar y$ be the images of $x_A,y_A$ under $S\otimes_k A\to S\otimes_k L$. Their product is zero by multiplicativity from Step 2. Their selected coordinates are the residues of $a_{i_0}$ and $b_{j_0}$. These are nonzero: each selected coefficient is a unit in $A$, since its inverse was adjoined, and a unital map to the nonzero field $L$ sends a unit to a unit. By the coordinate uniqueness in Step 2, $\bar x\ne0$ and $\bar y\ne0$. This contradicts the hypothesis that $S\otimes_k L$ is a domain. Hence $S\otimes_k K$ has no nonzero zero divisors; Step 2 already proved it nonzero. Since $K/k$ was arbitrary, the conclusion follows.
